context:
Extend the existing docs.yml workflow rather than creating a separate workflow.
This ensures atomic site assembly: all components (landing, docs, blog, explorer)
are built in one workflow run and deployed together. The explorer build is
additive - it adds steps but doesn't change existing ones.
description:
Wire the results explorer into the existing GitHub Pages deployment so that
a single `git push` to `main` builds and deploys the complete site:
landing page + Sphinx docs + blog + results explorer.

This TODO modifies `.github/workflows/docs.yml` (or adds a companion workflow)
to include the explorer build steps: run the static build pipeline, build the
Vite app, and assemble the output into the `/site/results/` directory.

It also adds the "Results" link to the shared site navigation so users can
discover the explorer from any page on benchbox.dev.

anti_patterns.dont: create a separate GitHub Pages deployment for the explorer
anti_patterns.why: GitHub Pages supports only one source per repo

anti_patterns.dont: let explorer build failures silently skip deployment
anti_patterns.why: a broken explorer should block deployment

preserves.behavior: Existing docs workflow jobs (linkcheck, spellcheck, example-validation, docstring-coverage) must not be affected
Existing landing page, Sphinx docs, and blog must continue to build and deploy correctly
GitHub Pages deployment must remain a single atomic upload (not multiple competing deployments)

verifications.description: Full site builds successfully in CI
Explorer pages are present in assembled site

work_units.notes:
Modify `.github/workflows/docs.yml` so the workflow also triggers on
`results-explorer/**` and `results-data/**`, then add build steps after the
existing Sphinx build:

1. Set up Node.js (v20+)
2. Install explorer dependencies: `cd results-explorer && npm ci`
3. Run static build pipeline: `uv run -- python scripts/build_read_model.py --input results-data/bundles/ --output results-explorer/public/data/`
4. Build explorer: `cd results-explorer && npm run build`
5. Copy explorer output to site assembly: `mkdir -p site/results && cp -R results-explorer/dist/. site/results/`

The step order matters: pipeline must run before Vite build (Vite needs data
files in `public/data/`), and explorer copy must happen before the Pages
upload action.

Consider caching `node_modules` and `.duckdb` artifacts for faster CI.
work_units.summary: Add explorer build steps to the GitHub Pages workflow

work_units.notes:
GitHub Pages serves 404.html for unknown paths. For the explorer's
client-side routes (especially compare view with query params), add a
`404.html` in the `results/` directory that:
1. Detects if the URL is a valid explorer route
2. If yes, loads the explorer app and handles routing client-side
3. If no, shows a friendly "result not found" page

Alternatively, if all routes are pre-rendered at build time, the 404
only needs to handle truly invalid paths. Test both scenarios.

Before merging to main:
1. Push to a test branch with GitHub Pages enabled
2. Verify the full site deploys: landing + docs + blog + explorer
3. Verify all explorer pages load correctly:
   - /results/ (home)
   - /results/tpch/ (benchmark index)
   - /results/duckdb/ (platform index)
   - /results/r/{id} (detail page)
   - /results/compare?ids=a,b (compare view)
4. Verify DuckDB-WASM loads and filtering works
5. Verify raw bundle download links work
6. Test on Chrome, Firefox, Safari
7. Check that existing docs, landing, and blog pages are unaffected
work_units.summary: End-to-end deployment test on a staging branch
